title: Ines and the Ember
premise: Ada Blackwood, a mercenary bound to the silent god Veth and keeper of ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent years staying invisible—until the border wards collapse, the stars go out, and a girl named Ines arrives clutching an ember that burns without heat: the last spark of her brother's soul, sold to the court beneath the mountain. To reclaim it, Ada must break every rule of their guild, gather a found family of debtors and deserters, and bargain with a god who no longer answers. The climax comes in the court beneath the mountain, where Ada learns Veth went silent because it was imprisoned there—and that freeing it means surrendering their own name to the ledger of souls. Ada pays the price, Ines's brother is restored, and the guild becomes something new: not invisible, but accountable.
about_author: L. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing legal documents about debts, inheritances, and disputes, which explains the obsession with ledgers that runs through all their fiction. They live near a mountain they refuse to go under.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On inventory night at the Guild of Impossible Things, the stars vanish one by one and the border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass. Ada locks the doors, checks the ledgers, and finds one entry glowing faintly: a soul, sold, unpaid. Emotional beat: dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: A Girl with an Ember
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ines, eleven years old and furious, breaks into the guild demanding they honor a contract her dead mother signed—her brother's soul was collateral, and she carries its ember in a tin box. Ada wants to turn her away; the ember recognizes them instead. Beat: reluctant responsibility kindling.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with flashbacks. We learn how Ada swore to Veth, the quiet god of debts and mercy, and why the guild trades in what shouldn't be owned. The ledger shows Ines's brother's soul was bought by the court beneath the mountain—paid for with something Ada once lost. Beat: guilt surfaces.

chapters.title: The Debtors' Table
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ada convenes the guild's strangest members: Marrow, a debt-collector ghost; Sefa, a cartographer of places that move; Old Brannic, who owes the guild his death and keeps postponing it. Ada asks for help breaking guild law. Most refuse. Beat: loneliness of leadership.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Keeping Out
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She maps the fallen wards and discovers they weren't keeping raiders out—they were keeping the court beneath the mountain from collecting on old bargains. The starless night is a repossession. Beat: the scale of the threat becomes clear.

chapters.title: Prayers Returned Unopened
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada prays to Veth for the first time in years and receives silence—but the ember flares when they speak aloud, as if the girl's brother can hear. Ines overhears and accuses Ada of abandoning her god just like everyone abandoned her. Beat: bitter honesty between them.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ada, Ines, Sefa, and Brannic set out along a road that erases travelers' memories as payment for passage. Ines clings to memories of her brother; Ada lets pieces of their past go too easily, which frightens her more than losing them. Beat: what we choose to forget.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Marrow's POV. At a bridge guarded by a toll-keeper who takes names instead of coin, Marrow reveals he once worked for the court below and deserted. He offers himself as guide in exchange for erasure of his own debt. Beat: found family begins to form around shared shame.

chapters.title: Ash Market
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The party passes through a market where memories, years, and shadows are traded. Ada sells a memory of Veth's voice to buy passage for Ines—and immediately mourns it. A court agent marks them. Beat: sacrifice made casually, regretted deeply.

chapters.title: The Agent in Grey
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The court's collector catches up and offers Ada a deal: deliver the ember willingly and Ines goes free. Ada refuses, and the agent reveals Veth didn't go silent—it was taken, chained beneath the mountain for forgiving debts too freely. Beat: the quest doubles; now it's rescue.

chapters.title: Brannic's Last Good Night
chapters.summary: Old Brannic's POV. Knowing the road ahead will kill him, Brannic finally accepts the death he's owed—on his own terms, buying the party safe passage through a cursed pass. His goodbye dinner is funny, warm, and devastating. Beat: grief as a gift freely given.

chapters.title: Under the Mountain's Skin
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The survivors enter the mountain through a wound in its side. The tunnels are lined with shelved souls, humming. The ember pulls toward its brother like a compass needle. Ines admits she's terrified Ada will trade her away. Beat: trust tested by fear.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They reach the court: a bureaucracy of the dead where souls are filed, audited, and forgotten. Ada uses their guild knowledge to forge credentials, walking the line between infiltration and becoming what they hate. Beat: complicity and cunning intertwined.

chapters.title: Audience with the Auditor
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Auditor, faceless and polite, reviews Ines's claim and finds it valid—but payment requires a soul of equal weight. The party realizes someone must stay. Ines volunteers before anyone can stop her. Beat: horror at a child's self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Chained God
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the ember's pull deeper, Ada finds Veth—not silent, but shackled, its voice stolen into the court's ledgers. Veth shows Ada the truth: it forgave Ada's original debt long ago, and Ada has been serving a god who asked nothing back. Beat: grace, undeserved and unbearable.

chapters.title: Amendment to the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada proposes the impossible: amend the court's own books, transferring Veth's imprisonment onto a willing signer. The clause requires a name surrendered forever. Ada signs before the others can argue. Beat: quiet, resolute self-loss.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. As the amendment takes hold, Ada begins to fade from memory and record—Ines fights to hold onto their face, screaming their name into the dark so someone will remember. Veth rises, unchained, and the mountain groans. Beat: love against erasure.

chapters.title: When the Stars Came Back
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Freed, Veth unmakes the court's claims; souls pour home like birds. The stars reignite over a world waking to returned wards and returned people. But Ada is gone from every ledger—including the guild's. Beat: triumph shadowed by absence.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Back at the guild, the members rebuild, honoring Brannic and mourning Ada. Ines refuses to accept the loss, rereading every page of the ledgers looking for loopholes—because if anyone could survive being erased, it would be Ada. Beat: hope as stubborn practice.

chapters.title: An Entry in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines finds a new entry in the oldest ledger, written in handwriting she knows: a debt owed to a girl with an ember, payable in person. Veth appears and tells her where names go when they're surrendered—not destroyed, only held. Beat: desperate, trembling hope confirmed.

chapters.title: Ines and the Ember
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climax. Ines descends alone to the place where surrendered names are kept, carrying the ember—which still holds a fragment of her brother's warmth—as proof of what love can redeem. She argues with the dark itself, using everything Ada taught her about contracts. Beat: courage inherited, not given.

chapters.title: Payable in Person
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, resolution. Ada wakes at the guild door with no memory of the mountain but a name restored, and finds Ines waiting with the ledger open. The guild reopens under new rules: nothing impossible gets bought, only returned. Beat: homecoming, family chosen twice.
